metadata.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning (He, Fan, Wu, Xie, Girshick, 2019)
metadata.framework: contrastive learning with momentum-updated key encoder and queue of negatives
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1911.05722.

nodes.name: Contrastive learning as dictionary lookup
nodes.statement: Contrastive unsupervised learning builds dynamic dictionaries. A query $q$ is encoded from one augmented view of an image; keys $\{k_0, k_1, \ldots\}$ are encoded from other views. The positive key $k_+$ comes from a different augmentation of the same image; negative keys come from different images. The goal is to learn representations where $q$ is similar to $k_+$ and dissimilar to negatives.

nodes.name: InfoNCE loss
nodes.statement: The InfoNCE contrastive loss: $\mathcal{L}_q = -\log \frac{\exp(q \cdot k_+ / \tau)}{\sum_{i=0}^{K} \exp(q \cdot k_i / \tau)}$ where $\tau > 0$ is a temperature hyperparameter, $k_+$ is the positive key, and $\{k_i\}_{i=0}^K$ includes $k_+$ and $K$ negative keys. This is equivalent to a $(K+1)$-way softmax classification of $q$ as belonging to class $k_+$.

nodes.name: Momentum-updated key encoder
nodes.statement: The query encoder $f_q$ with parameters $\theta_q$ is updated by backpropagation. The key encoder $f_k$ with parameters $\theta_k$ is NOT updated by gradient but by exponential moving average (momentum update): $\theta_k \leftarrow m \theta_k + (1 - m) \theta_q$ with momentum coefficient $m \in [0,1)$ (e.g., $m = 0.999$). This provides slowly evolving, consistent key representations.

nodes.name: Queue of negative keys
nodes.statement: Maintain a queue (FIFO) of the most recent mini-batches' encoded keys. The current mini-batch is enqueued and the oldest batch is dequeued. This decouples the dictionary size $K$ from the mini-batch size, allowing a very large number of negatives (e.g., $K = 65536$) without requiring large batch sizes.

nodes.name: MoCo algorithm
nodes.statement: MoCo training: (1) Sample a mini-batch of images, create two random augmentations per image. (2) Encode queries via $f_q$; encode keys via $f_k$ (no gradient). (3) Compute InfoNCE loss with positive pair + queue negatives. (4) Update $\theta_q$ by SGD; update $\theta_k$ by momentum. (5) Enqueue current keys, dequeue oldest.

nodes.name: Large consistent dictionary enables better representations
nodes.statement: The momentum update is critical: using $m=0.999$ significantly outperforms end-to-end training of both encoders ($m=0$, equivalent to no momentum). The queue enables dictionary sizes of 65K negatives, far larger than the batch size. On ImageNet linear probing, MoCo achieves 60.6% top-1 accuracy with a ResNet-50 encoder, competitive with supervised pre-training for downstream transfer tasks.
conclusions: Momentum update crucial for dictionary consistency
Competitive with supervised pre-training on transfer tasks
